title: Emerging jets with a track transformer tagger (Delphes ATLAS example)
short: Two-jet search for dark-QCD emerging jets, selected with a transformer tagger on displaced tracks.
description_html:
This example analysis mimics a search for emerging jets: jets of dark-sector hadrons that decay back to Standard Model particles a short distance from the collision point, producing many tracks with large impact parameter. The detector-level selection uses a transformer tagger that reads the tracks associated to each large-radius jet and scores how emerging-jet-like the jet is.

The detector response is simulated with Delphes using an ATLAS-like card with track smearing. The surrogate was trained on the same simulated samples, but sees only the generator-level (truth) particles of each jet.
signal_region: Events with at least two large-radius truth jets with pT > 200 GeV and |eta| < 2.5 whose tagger score passes the working point with a QCD rejection of 1000. The efficiency is the fraction of your events that pass this selection.
inputs: HepMC2 or HepMC3 ASCII, generator level (no detector simulation), optionally gzipped
Stable final-state particles with production vertices, plus the dark-sector hadrons and their decay vertices

references.label: arXiv:2505.02429, Search for emerging jets in pp collisions at 13.6 TeV with the ATLAS experiment
Delphes 3, a modular framework for fast simulation of a generic collider experiment

figures.caption: Signal-region efficiency versus dark-pion lifetime for m_pid = 5 GeV. Full Delphes chain (points) compared with the surrogate prediction on generator truth (band).
Distribution of the per-jet tagger score at detector level compared with the surrogate probability on truth jets, for the nominal signal sample.

model.training: Trained on 1M QCD and 1M signal events (3 lifetimes, 34 seeds) generated with Pythia 8 and Delphes. Targets are the detector-level tagger decisions at the 1000 QCD rejection working point. Validated on held-out lifetimes and two alternative dark-pion masses.
